query: Nice point to add in your Nuwara Eliya Journey This place is for nature lovers. This is very nice farm and around this, you will see lot of beautiful nature. This is a must place for photo addict. You will be loving the climate. Keep one whole day for this area as you will not feel how time will spend while watching at natural beauty

Worth a visit It's a one hour ride by bike from Anuradhapura and an approx. 20 minutes walk up. Entrance fee is Rs. 500 and on the top you'll habe the chance to go up to three different peaks. We enjoyed the one with the dagoba most. Btw: There's some maintenance work going on at the moment, bit still wort a visit.

Could have been interesting Part of a tour group (22 people) but the museum not designed for a group of that size and the lack of space, speed of presentation & the guides accent made interpreting the various masks on display very difficult. There are story boards with the masks but not given the time to view/read them. The masks that were on display were very colourfu, unique and interesting - lots of detail on carving & painting. After leaving the downstairs museum there is a chance to view the actual carving and painting of the masks and this was quite interesting seeing them omoving from a single block of wood to the end product. Could have been much more interesting if group size wa slimited to 10 or so guests.

Great surfing place Is the best spot on the east coast to surf, if you’re willing to take a bath you can try but the waves are too strong to let you easily go in the sea, there are a lot of cheap bars where you can drink and eat after you had a surfing day
Paradise Bentota beach is the perfect place if you are looking for a quiet place. You can rent a sun bed and an umbrella for a few dollars. The beach is clean with warm water.

Solo This park was the alternative to Yala due to the Jeep drivers strike. Ok if you like birds but no leopards, bears and only one elephant. Plus we had a park guide that was not very knowledgeable and was difficult to understand. Save your money if Yala is still closed.

Quite interesting We were shown all the old machines and the process the tea leaves went through to end up in our cup. Floors 2 and 3 didnt have much and the top floor was where you got your cup of tea

Heartfelt experience Based in the shell of the house of one of the tsunami survivors in hikkaduwa is this very real and sobering experience of many survivors, from mothers that lost their children, children that were orphaned as well as people that are still looking for loved ones as their bodies were never found. The photos, stories and even pictures drawn by small children all help to piece together the tragic events that took place. A really humbling experience.
Amazing Fully operating tea factory. Great tour through each stage of the process. Clothes smelled of tea after visit! Must visit if checking out Lipton seat

Well worth a visit Certainly worth a visit when visiting the region and can be easily included as part of a visit to Sigiriya etc. The frescos and Buddha shrines are located in the series of caves and are can be seen quite well from the lighting supplied. Flash photography is not condoned so taking pictures can be a challenge. You will have to remove your shoes and have clothes that cover your legs and shoulders.

Need the rainy season The Diyaluma Falls can be seen from afar as you approach them travelling from Wellawaya to Beragala. We have seen these falls on many occasions but strongly advise, if possible, to visit during the wet season when they are spectacular. On this occasion (January) we remained impressed by the incredible height of the falls but the volume of water was very low. There are places to get water, drinks and snacks on the roadside at the foot of the falls. If travelling this road, it is worth stopping to enjoy the incredible power of nature.

Full with wildlife Beautiful park with a lot of wildlife. The road to the park is already beautiful. You can do this strech with a scooter (though there are big elephants present!) or tuktuk and can see everything except maybe the leopard. But the park is worth the extra money. Scenery is very nice. Many birds, eliphants, crocodiles, fox, deer and many more. We saw within 10 minutes a big leopard.
nice place to visit well worth a look big place to walk around great view of cricket ground over the road many shops bars etc here we came back on a night for a meal and loved it

Tourist Trap A tourist trap. One is quickly shown around the rather smallish factory. Complimentary tea and then ushered to a rather pricy factory store. Where products are sold at double the price. I will suggest one goes there sees the factory and not buy anything. Also I think the driver or tour operator gets a cut here. Also the packaging does not have manufacturing date or product details.

An absolutely hidden gem! Well worth the visit! Never ever did we have any idea about tea and just what was required! This was an absolutely hidden gem and was just amazing. Thoroughly recommend this as a visit. Actually got to see tea being sorted and then tasted the product you just can’t ask for more!!!
Nice Staff Great place to visit. The staff are very friendly and knowledgeable. They're doing an amazing cause for the sea turtles.

Not a good museum, but definitely a good experience. From a museums perspective, this museum is not good. Each exhibit is based on one of the participating Buddhist countries and varies widely in quality and perspective. Each overly dense word panel seems written by a bureaucratic functionary from the embassy with overly careful attention to lauding that country's buddhist tradition. Biases are laid bare: the Thailand exhibit suggests that their King is a Bhoddisatva (a kind of Buddhist saint) and calls him the "King of Kings"; the Tibetan exhibit is a part of the Chinese exhibit and *never once mentions the Dali Lama.* Did you catch that? The "World Buddhist Museum" *does not mention the Dali Lama! So no, this is not a good museum. it is a terrible museum. But it is a great experience! As long as you approach it knowing that each exhibit is a state-sponsored piece of propoganda written by people with understanding of museum principles, it becomes an unintentional museum of buddhist propaganda! The the main entryway's exhibit on the Buddha's teachings was really quite moving - powerful and simple moral messages to live by - which, like Western tradition's Ten Commandment, none of the countries espousing them follow them particularly well.

A slice of history This was a revisit after 4 years. Little progress has been made on the governor's house, which was disappointing. There was also no one in attendance who could speak English so our questions went unanswered. The fort itself is a truly magnificent testement to its builders.

A must for anyone interested in Buddhism or history! To see the tree grown from a sapling of the original Bodhi tree in Lumpini, Nepal, where the Buddha achieved enlightenment and that was brought here by King Asoka's daughter and planted in 288 BC, is truly overwhelming and yet soothing and totally mesmerizing, indeed. It's the oldest tree of its kind in the world, and it's been attended to by appointed care-givers since that time.

Great setting - but I hope they clean it The walk there is cool and should be combined with peace pagoda, then once there its really junglish and cool - but oh so dirty. No fun to swim with the dirt. Note that the bar on the beach is closed since covid and has been reclaimed by nature.

Very easy and pleasant walk Walking around the lake was an extremely pleasant way to spend an afternoon . The only issue is that is is almost impossible to cross the road to gain access to a number of restaurants on the south side of the lake.

Amazing herds of elephants with babies Fabulous trip organised from guesthouse. Picked up and taken to where the herds had migrated to in the parks. Spent a couple hours just watching the elephants. Jeeps kept to the roads and are only supposed to park on sode of road to preserve the grass. The elephants seem to like grazing near the roads instead of at a distance which was great. Baby elephants everywhere! We tipped the drivers at the end for a good job done.
Nice place, cool and lots of things to do We were in Nuwara Eliya for one night, we visited the lake and had a boat ride, there are lots of fun thrill seeking activities here.

Sunrise tuk tuk ride! Picked up at 0500am got there 0545am. Views were amazing, definitely recommend the early get up as it was clear and the clouds started rolling in 9ish. 1000 for a tuk tuk up to the Seat. Lovely walk to the tea factory on the way down and he will wait there and return journey 500 to Haputale! And the rotis and tea are a big plus from the ‘cafe’ at the top.

Not a bad afternoon stroll Worth a visit if you are heading towards Pedros Tea Factory, but we didn't find this waterfall particularly special. A nice easy half an hour walk through the tea plantation (from the factory), and up a rocky terrain towards the end. The walk itself was enjoyable, and the waterfall was pretty, but plenty more spectacular sites elsewhere in the Hill Country. That being said, would still recommend this as a peaceful way to spend an afternoon, paired with Pedros Tea Factory.

Nice little exibit from late Martin Wickramasinghe That is a great place to visit if you want to get an idea of life in Sri Lanka 100 years ago. One of the best writers, SrI lanka was ever gifted. The place is really beautiful. Please do not visit this palce if you do not want to see southern Sri Lankan village 100 years ago.
Great afternoon safari Spent an afternoon in the park Saw soo many elephants With many calfs playing A special experience not to be missed during the gathering

Average; foreigners, beware! Visited this place when I had a few hours to kill in Colombo. The entrance fee of Rs.1000 was too high in my opinion. The collections of the museum vary from very average to somewhat interesting. Some more contemporary displays would have been nice. Foreigners: beware of the cafeteria. I asked for a chocolate drink that I was told cost Rs.150. Paid 500, but was shortchanged by 100. I had to ask for this extra money. Moreover, upon finishing the drink, I noticed it was labelled 50, not 150. Again, I had to request that I be given an extra 100 back that I was duly owed. The two apologies from the cashier were very insincere, and it is therefore regrettable to experience the extent to which they went to try and rip me, a foreign tourist, off. This is from a government owned museum. Shameful. Upon leaving, I was asked to complete a survey. Apparently staff members within the exhibitions are meant to chat to you about their various displays, however, I can only say this was the case with 1 single staff member! Nevertheless, the woman conducting the survey was very friendly, and provided me with very detailed instructions on taking the bus back to my hotel. This was a very positive note to end on.
Good place Had fun with family. But after when we were done we couldn't find a cab. Also most of areas were under renovation.

Spice of life A real interesting visit here ,a guide around the spice plants with informative information in relation to how natural plants can be substituted for other chemist medicines and food preparation. So much explained it was hard to take it all in ,complimentary head and back massage which was very good . At the end of tour talk a lot of people including myself visited the shop and purchased some of the items .I bought a oil rub and paste for arthritis in my shoulder and it still is providing some relief and benefit . Overall a interesting experience.

Beautiful young corals Lovely to see so many healthy young corals growing and I esp enjoyed seeing the sharks. I half dived half snorkelled during my trip. Pigeon island gets really busy for a more interesting experience you might want to consider scuba diving with Nilaveli Diving Centre at nearby Crow island - some great coral & lots of underwater life.
Elephants close up The elephants were a delight and watching them splash around in the river was amazing. 3 hours from Colombo with interesting road sights and villages along the way

A vast area of ancient sacred places Our knowledgeable driver was our guide to this fascinating area. On the day we visited it was popular with Sri Lankan school visitors who arrived in lots of coaches. The pupils were dressed in the common white school uniforms and dresses. It was very very hot but cold drinks could be obtained from stalls near the entrances. In the sacred areas you must remove footwear so remember to wear socks to protect your feet otherwise you could be dancing on the hot stones.

Great spot for a dip Walk right up to the viewing platform first to get a good photo of the falls, then back down to the base of the main falls. Put on swimmies, then go for a dook. Chilly at first, but warms up. Deepest on the left, and can swim about a bit. Before heading back, go immediately down river from the main falls (it's a bit slippy in places) for an amazing view. If you scramble down a bit there's another pool there. Head down the path and about half way down there's another great pool for a dip. The whole thing is sublime.

Amazing waterfall Beautiful waterfall but it's right on a main road so not a peaceful place to visit. Worth stopping off in a tuk tuk on your way to the coast for the view. Would not recommend walking here from town as the road is not safe to walk on.

Calm and beautiful The royal botanical gardens are beautifully maintained and we have a chance to see so many different varieties of trees and plants from different parts of the world. The kids had a great time there and there was a beautiful lake shaped like Srilanka. We got to see different palm varieties and the double coconut tree.

Worth the climb Even though I didn't claimed the rock I regret that for not going when the kids returned with dad after climbing the rock. They had taken bunch of pictures and they looked amazing. During the day time sun is too much so use a sun screen otherwise you'll get sun burn.

Well maintained This museum at the entrance of the complex gives us a birds eye view of what we are going to see in the sigiriya rock fortress. Better to visit this place to know the historical aspects, especially if you are NOT engaging a guide.

Nice part of the beautiful countryside in Nuwara Eliya area We were on a tour bus en route to the Pedro Tea Gardens and stopped to photograph this lovely part of the local scenery. It's not a "knockout" but it is quite beautiful.
Amaizing Temple One of the best temple during the tour. The elephant was well discipline. Heard that it was used for the scared pageant.
A breath of fresh air Pay a small entry fee. Lovely space for the children to enjoy and the gardens are well maintained. A highlight in Nuwara Eliya.

Serendipity If you are there at the right place at the right time, then you see the lot. In one afternoon safari, we were so fortunate to see leopards, sloth bear, elephants, wild boars, water buffalo's, mongoose, star tortoise, barking and spotted deer and lots of birds, It was our lucky day, hope they will be still there for our next visit to the park and the Tree House at the Wilpattu Corridor.
